title: arXiv AI — notable papers from the 2026-10-15 announcement batch
global_caveat: arXiv has no official trending chart. This is an editorial relevance ranking of notable recent papers, not a popularity ranking; all eight selected Semantic Scholar records had zero citations at the 2026-10-16 00:13 UTC snapshot.

sections.title: Why Do Agent Teams Fail Across Boundaries? A Failure Taxonomy for Agent-to-Agent Systems with Private States
sections.abstract: Studies how agents acting for different principals fail when they have private states and mixed incentives, deriving a taxonomy from more than 2,500 runs across 488 scenarios.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors derive 20 A2A failure modes in discovery/delegation, grounding/record consistency, verification, and conduct/fidelity, and argue for scoring agents against their own objectives as well as task outcomes.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors say automated analysis-agent tagging may have missed failure modes, despite human validation.

sections.title: Co-Evolving Acting and Forecasting for Language Agents
sections.abstract: Adds multi-step future-action prediction as training supervision for language agents, reporting stronger aggregate results across five benchmarks and up to 1.9×–2.0× sample-efficiency gains on ScienceWorld.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors' CoPE objective teaches a single policy backbone to forecast action sequences from prior histories while still acting one step at a time, without extra inference overhead.
sections.unique_caveat: The full paper reports mixed results on τ²-Bench: an improvement on Retail but a decline on Airline.

sections.title: SafeDriveVLA: Navigation-Conditioned World Model Dreaming for Conflict-Aware End-to-End Autonomous Driving
sections.abstract: Introduces a benchmark and VLA driving method for handling unsafe conflicts between free-form navigation instructions and the observed road scene.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors introduce a three-mode navigation-compliance predictor informed by a world model that imagines strict instruction-following, to decide when the instruction is safe.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors note that benchmark driving modes are inferred from expert trajectories, prompts come from fixed paraphrase pools, and the world-model anchor does not encode speed.

sections.title: Asymptotic Behavior of Transformers
sections.abstract: Analyzes long-run text generation, showing that some small transformers fail to converge while a specified richer class converges above a model-dependent softmax-temperature threshold.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors establish a convergence threshold for every transformer in their analyzed class, while proving that no single finite temperature threshold works uniformly across the whole class.
sections.unique_caveat: The convergence guarantee is conditional on the paper's model class and temperature threshold; it is not a blanket guarantee for arbitrary deployed language models.

sections.title: When Is Smaller Greener? Right-Sizing Language Models for Agentic AI
sections.abstract: Proposes choosing models by energy, cost, and time per successfully completed agent task rather than per call, and reports task-length crossovers in a pilot study.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors derive a decision framework for model selection using task-level resource costs, with a Pareto screen before preference-based trade-offs.
sections.unique_caveat: The empirical pilot covers 15 open-weight models but only two multi-step agent tasks; broader hardware and task coverage remains unshown in the abstract.

sections.title: GeoThinker-$F$: Endogenous Predictive World Representations for Fast Spatial Intelligence
sections.abstract: Trains a multimodal model to predict and use latent spatial priors internally, removing runtime dependence on an external 3D encoder while reporting up to 3.6× inference speedup.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors use latent frame-prediction heads and spatial-grounded temporal fusion so the MLLM can supply useful geometry and future-semantic priors without running the external geometry expert at inference.
sections.unique_caveat: The abstract reports competitive benchmark performance and a best-case speedup; it does not establish equivalent gains across every benchmark or real-world deployment.

sections.title: VITAL: From Visual Motion to Precise Action
sections.abstract: Encodes trajectories as a visual-motion scaffold plus a compact residual, reporting near-matched NAVSIM performance with one denoising step and 3.29× end-to-end inference speed.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors train an action expert to predict a visually derived motion scaffold and a normalized trajectory-error residual, then refine the residual with bounded reinforcement post-training.
sections.unique_caveat: The reported evidence is benchmark-based; the abstract does not demonstrate real-world closed-loop driving.

sections.title: LLM-jp-4 Technical Report
sections.abstract: Reports an 8B dense and 32B-A3B Japanese model family trained from scratch on about 12 trillion tokens, with an emphasis on transparent and reproducible development.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors present the LLM-jp-4 family and document their data, external-model, software, and training choices to support independent scrutiny.
sections.unique_caveat: The abstract reports competitive results against similarly sized open-weight models; it does not itself establish independent reproduction or broad superiority.
